german: die drei literarischen Gattungen (Epik, Lyrik, Dramatik)
english: the three literary genres (narrative, poetry, drama)
note: The traditional top-level division of literature into three genres — every specific form (Roman, Gedicht, Drama …) belongs to one of them.

examples.de: Die drei literarischen Gattungen sind Epik, Lyrik und Dramatik.
examples.en: The three literary genres are narrative prose, poetry, and drama.

note: The genre told in prose, with a narrator — includes the novel, the shorter Erzählung, and the even more compact Kurzgeschichte.

examples.de: Zur Epik zählen Roman, Erzählung und Kurzgeschichte.
examples.en: Narrative prose includes the novel, the tale, and the short story.

note: The genre built from compressed, often rhythmic or rhymed language — organised into Verse (lines) and Strophen (stanzas).

examples.de: Die Lyrik arbeitet mit Vers, Strophe und Reim.
examples.en: Poetry works with the verse line, the stanza, and rhyme.

note: The genre written to be performed — structured into Akte (acts) and Szenen (scenes), carried almost entirely by Dialog.

examples.de: Ein Drama gliedert sich in Akte und Szenen.
examples.en: A play is structured into acts and scenes.

note: The longest common prose form — der historische Roman, der Bildungsroman, der Kriminalroman.

examples.de: Der Roman spielt im Berlin der 1920er Jahre.
examples.en: The novel is set in the Berlin of the 1920s.

note: Who tells the story and how much they know — the single choice that shapes what the reader is allowed to find out.

examples.de: Die Erzählperspektive bestimmt, was der Leser wissen kann.
examples.en: The narrative perspective determines what the reader can know.

note: A narrator who stands outside the story and knows everything — every character's thoughts, the past and future, sometimes commenting directly to the reader.

examples.de: Ein auktorialer Erzähler kennt die Gedanken aller Figuren.
examples.en: An omniscient narrator knows the thoughts of every character.

note: A narrator who is also a character in the story, telling it from their own limited point of view.

examples.de: Der Ich-Erzähler schildert die Ereignisse aus seiner eigenen Sicht.
examples.en: The first-person narrator describes the events from his own perspective.

note: A third-person narrator whose knowledge is limited to one character's perspective — unlike the auktorial narrator, who sees everything.

examples.de: Ein personaler Erzähler bleibt eng an der Perspektive einer einzigen Figur.
examples.en: A close third-person narrator stays tightly bound to a single character's perspective.

note: A narrator whose account the reader has reason to doubt — through gaps, contradictions, or a clear bias — a favourite device for building interpretive uncertainty.

examples.de: Ein unzuverlässiger Erzähler lässt Zweifel an der eigenen Darstellung aufkommen.
examples.en: An unreliable narrator raises doubts about their own account.

note: A jump backward in the timeline to show earlier events — interrupts the main Handlung to fill in context.

examples.de: Eine Rückblende unterbricht die Handlung, um Vergangenes zu zeigen.
examples.en: A flashback interrupts the plot to show past events.

note: The umbrella term for any deliberate linguistic technique used for effect — Metapher, Symbol, and Ironie are all Stilmittel.

examples.de: Metapher und Ironie sind klassische Stilmittel.
examples.en: Metaphor and irony are classic stylistic devices.

note: A word or image transferred from one thing to describe another, without "like" or "as" — das Leben ist eine Reise.

examples.de: In der Metapher "das Leben ist eine Reise" wird ein Bild auf einen anderen Sachverhalt übertragen.
examples.en: In the metaphor "life is a journey," an image is transferred onto another subject.

note: An object or image that stands for something beyond its literal meaning — die Rose als Symbol der Liebe.

examples.de: Die Rose steht symbolisch für vergängliche Schönheit.
examples.en: The rose symbolically represents fleeting beauty.

note: A recurring image, idea, or situation that runs through a work — distinct from a Symbol, which is a single object standing for a meaning.

examples.de: Das Motiv der Einsamkeit zieht sich durch den ganzen Roman.
examples.en: The motif of loneliness runs through the entire novel.

note: Saying or implying the opposite of the literal meaning — often signals the narrator's distance from what's being described.

examples.de: Die Ironie des Erzählers zeigt sich in seinem distanzierten Ton.
examples.en: The narrator's irony shows in his detached tone.

note: A specific kind of Motiv that recurs deliberately at key moments, often signalling a theme each time it returns.

examples.de: Ein Leitmotiv kehrt an mehreren Stellen des Werks wieder.
examples.en: A leitmotif returns at several points in the work.

note: To explain what a text means, beyond its literal content — den Text interpretieren.

examples.de: Der Text lässt sich auf verschiedene Weisen interpretieren.
examples.en: The text can be interpreted in different ways.

english: to interpret, to read as meaning
note: Close to interpretieren, but leans toward a more suggestive, intuitive reading — often used for a single ambiguous detail rather than a whole text.

examples.de: Kritiker deuten das Ende des Romans als offenen Schluss.
examples.en: Critics read the novel's ending as an open ending.

note: The essay genre that examines a text's structure, language, and effect — the C1 exam task this unit's vocabulary is built for.

examples.de: Eine Textanalyse untersucht Aufbau, Sprache und Wirkung eines Werks.
examples.en: A text analysis examines a work's structure, language, and effect.

note: How tension rises and falls across a work — der Spannungsbogen steigt/erreicht seinen Höhepunkt.

examples.de: Der Spannungsbogen erreicht seinen Höhepunkt im letzten Kapitel.
examples.en: The dramatic arc reaches its peak in the final chapter.

note: The moment the plot's direction changes decisively — often where the Spannungsbogen shifts.

examples.de: Am Wendepunkt der Handlung ändert sich alles.
examples.en: At the turning point of the plot, everything changes.

note: The sequence of events that make up the story — die Handlung spielt in/zusammenfassen.

examples.de: Die Handlung spielt über mehrere Jahrzehnte hinweg.
examples.en: The plot spans several decades.

note: A person in a story — die Hauptfigur, die Nebenfigur — distinct from the everyday sense of Figur meaning "build/physique."

examples.de: Die Hauptfigur entwickelt sich im Laufe der Handlung stark.
examples.en: The main character develops significantly over the course of the plot.

note: The central character a story follows — close to Hauptfigur, but a more formal, analysis-register term.

examples.de: Der Protagonist steht im Zentrum der Erzählung.
examples.en: The protagonist stands at the centre of the narrative.

note: A named stretch of literary history with shared characteristics — die Epoche der Klassik, der Romantik, des Expressionismus.

examples.de: Jede literarische Epoche hat ihre eigenen Merkmale.
examples.en: Every literary epoch has its own characteristics.

note: German-language literature written in the years directly after 1945, grappling with the war and its aftermath. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Nachkriegsliteratur verarbeitet die Erfahrungen des Krieges.
examples.en: Postwar literature works through the experiences of the war.

note: A specific strand of German postwar literature (late 1940s) depicting daily life amid the ruins of a destroyed country, in a stripped-down, unsentimental style. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Trümmerliteratur beschreibt schonungslos den Alltag im zerstörten Nachkriegsdeutschland.
examples.en: Rubble literature depicts, unsparingly, daily life in destroyed postwar Germany.
